The Speak Screen family on one product page — four related surfaces

Apple groups several Accessibility read-aloud features under Spoken Content. Western indie listings often mention one or more on the same US product page. AppLocale covers all four on this single guide — paste-ready zh-Hans copy for whichever your screenshots and description already claim:

  • Speak Screen (朗读屏幕) — system gesture or in-app equivalent that reads everything visible on screen aloud, top to bottom. Gallery frames may show a two-finger swipe demo, a floating read-aloud controller, or a "Listen to this page" badge.
  • Speak Selection (朗读所选内容) — highlight text and hear only the selection spoken. Screenshot overlays often show a context menu with Speak, copy-to-clipboard beside read-aloud, or selected paragraph playback.
  • Spoken Content settings (语音内容) — voice picker, speaking rate slider, pronunciation controls, and content-type preferences in Settings-style captures or in-app narration settings sheets.
  • Highlight Content while speaking (朗读时高亮) — words, sentences, or lines highlight in sync with playback. Marketing frames may show karaoke-style word tracking, sentence dimming, or line-by-line scroll during narration.

Your gallery may lead with Speak Screen on one frame and Highlight while speaking on the next. zh-Hans caption lines should name the correct surface per frame — a voice-rate slider is not a swipe-to-read gesture, and a highlight demo is not a Speak Selection menu unless that is what the screenshot shows.

Speak Screen-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Read-aloud marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Spoken Content workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Speak Screen vs Speak Selection vs generic TTS

US pages use "Speak Screen", "Read aloud", or "Listen to this page." China storefront copy often uses 朗读屏幕 for full-screen reading, 朗读所选内容 for selected-text playback, or 听读 / 朗读 for general narration — depending on whether you mean Apple's Accessibility feature name, in-app article playback, or ebook narration. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual read-aloud scope.

Spoken Content settings vs in-app voice picker

Screenshot galleries may show system Settings → Spoken Content (语音内容) separately from in-app voice and rate controls. Buyers distinguish system-wide Spoken Content from app-specific narration settings — match what your English listing and screenshots actually show.

Highlight while speaking vs plain playback

朗读时高亮 signals synchronized word or sentence highlighting during playback — a stronger claim than plain text-to-speech. Do not use highlight vocabulary on frames that only show a play button without visible word tracking.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need read-aloud search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 朗读屏幕, 朗读所选内容, and 听读 each signal different intent from Live Speech or VoiceOver keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Speak Screen" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Promotional text refreshes

Read-aloud feature launches and highlight-while-speaking updates often land in the 170-character promotional text field above the description — updatable without a new binary. See Promotional text in Simplified Chinese when your narration pitch lives in promo text rather than the long description.

AppLocale FAQ

Does AppLocale implement Speak Screen or Spoken Content APIs?

No. We deliver Connect listing metadata copy only — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot caption lines. AVSpeechSynthesizer integration, Spoken Content Accessibility API work, and read-aloud playback engineering are outside scope.

How is Speak Screen listing copy different from Live Speech?

Speak Screen listing copy covers read-aloud — the system or your app reads existing on-screen content aloud, including Speak Selection and highlight while speaking. Live Speech listing copy covers type-to-speak — users type custom phrases to speak aloud in conversations. Those are opposite content directions with different screenshot vocabulary.

How is this different from Personal Voice, VoiceOver, Dictation, or Live Caption?

Personal Voice covers on-device voice cloning for type-to-speak — a separate listing scope from read-aloud. VoiceOver covers screen reader navigation. Dictation covers speech-to-text into fields. Live Caption covers real-time subtitles for heard audio. Speak Screen reads visible text as audio — a different buyer story on each surface.

Only if your app actually provides that capability and your English listing already states it accurately. AppLocale rewrites from your source claims — we do not invent system-replacement promises or certify parity with Apple's Accessibility Spoken Content features.
